what_happened: Task 621's dispatch asked to 'create the typescript extension in full' but the extension already existed in full, fully committed by task 620's own implementation phases. Research pass confirmed all 20 files, the 4 python-lacks items, and zero lint/gate regressions, then executed the dispatch's own deferred VERIFICATION clause (end-to-end deploy test into a disposable scratch repo) which task 620 had explicitly scoped out -- confirming all three (plus a fourth, opencode_json, gated by an .managed marker) merge targets work correctly.

generate_opencode_json() in merge.lua silently no-ops (returns ok=true, writes nothing) when the target repo lacks an opencode.json.managed marker file -- undocumented in context/guides/extension-development.md or loader-reference.md. A future tester attempting to verify a new extension's opencode_json merge target against a fresh scratch repo will see apparent success with no file written and may misdiagnose it as broken rather than correctly gated.

Research pass had already executed the dispatch's VERIFICATION clause end-to-end (headless manager.load into a disposable scratch target) and confirmed all 20 files present and lint-clean, so the plan phase could size the remaining work as a 3-phase, 1.5h verification-closeout instead of re-authoring a full 20-file build plan. The report's opencode.json.managed gating discovery became a concrete Phase 2 task and a Phase 3 deliverable.
